decision.summary: Tenant wants to replace the landlord's broken LG washer with their own. This needs landlord consent, so I asked the landlord, noted the ticket, told the tenant what happens next, and set a follow-up for 29 July.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: At intake, with nothing decided. Outstanding: landlord consent, who pays removal and fitting, and what happens to the landlord's machine.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: The consent request has gone to the landlord (APR-101, via the agency landlord record). The tenant has been updated by email on the existing thread.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: Not an agency human. The landlord must decide on consent and cost because the machine is theirs. No escalation is needed yet.

conflicts: The intake classed this as a routine appliance repair, but the tenant is really asking to swap in their own appliance. I handled it as a landlord-consent request.
assumptions: Email on the existing thread is an acceptable tenant channel.

args.decision_needed: The tenant reports the LG washing machine (here when they moved in) has a power failure and, from their own web search, can't be fixed. They offer to buy a replacement at their own cost, which would stay their property and go with them when they leave; it would not be on the inventory. Do you consent? If so, who pays to disconnect and remove the existing machine and fit the new one, and what should happen to your machine (inspect, repair, or dispose)? Alternatively, we can send our contractor to inspect and repair/replace it.
options: Consent to tenant's own replacement (tenant's item stays theirs); tell us who pays removal/fitting and what to do with your machine
Send our contractor to inspect first

args.body: Hello, thanks for letting us know about the washing machine. Because the current machine belongs to the landlord, we need their consent before you swap it for your own. We've asked them, and put your terms to them: the new machine would be yours and you'd take it when you leave. We've also asked who covers removing the old one and fitting yours. Please don't remove the old machine yet. If you can, send a photo of the machine and any error code. We'll update you once the landlord replies, or by 29 July at the latest.
